article.title: China’s AI Industry Pivots to Agents From Models, Report Says
article.summary: China’s artificial intelligence industry is shifting from competition in large models and computing power toward the deployment and commercialization of AI agents, according to a report by the China Telecom Research Institute cited by China Central Television on Saturday.

article.title: OpenAI’s researchers burned $7,000 a day on AI agents — now it’s opening the floodgates
article.summary: OpenAI rolled out its Agents API in public beta Thursday, opening the backend behind Codex to developers looking to run agents unattended for days. Now, developers don’t have to build their own system to keep an agent going because the API keeps track of the job as it progresses and gives the agent somewhere to execute its work, even when a task stretches well beyond a single context window. Although that makes long-running agents easier to try, it also gives developers more ways to burn through compute. Interestingly enough, on the same day Agents API launched, OpenAI paused new sign-ups for its $200-a-month Pro plan after demand for GPT-6 Astra strained capacity. article.title: Google explains what’s going on with the disappearing speedometer in Maps on Android Auto
article.summary: TL;DR Google started bringing a live speedometer to Maps in Android Auto earlier this year. Earlier this week, some users reported no longer seeing the speedometer, as well as other map details. Google now explains that some users need to set a destination before the speedometer will appear. It’s a little shocking that it took until this summer for Google to start bringing a real-time speedometer to Maps on Android Auto , but better late than never! Combined with speed limit info in the app, that put some very useful information on Android Auto screens. And largely because we were so happy to see it finally arrive, we were particularly concerned earlier this week when we starting finding reports from users saying that it had suddenly vanished on them. article.title: Lenovo Googlebook 15 specs leak, and this clearly isn’t your schoolhouse Chromebook
article.summary: TL;DR Lenovo’s upcoming Googlebook 15 has reportedly leaked in full, revealing a 15.3-inch 120Hz OLED display, Intel Core Ultra 5 325 chip, and up to 32GB of RAM. The laptop could also feature a 70Wh battery, Wi-Fi 7, dual Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, a fingerprint reader, and a Google-colored battery/charging light on the lid. Googlebook OS will put Gemini Intelligence and Android phone integration front and center, while Lenovo is also preparing a dedicated Google key and an “AI Mouse” accessory. Earlier in May this year, Google introduced its Googlebook laptop category. These are laptops designed from the ground up for Gemini Intelligence, with Google aiming to create a PC experience that offers premium hardware, works seamlessly with Android phones, and puts AI features front and center.

article.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to ‘distill’ frontier models, too
article.summary: Tan wants smaller, American open-weight AI labs to use the same kind of training techniques on American frontier AI labs, giving the U.S. a more robust set of open-weight options that aren’t Chinese.

article.summary: I’m Matt Burns, Chief Content Officer at Insight Media Group. Each week, I round up the most important AI developments, explaining what they mean for people and organizations putting this technology to work. The thesis is simple: workers who learn to use AI will define the next era of their industries, and this newsletter is here to help you be one of them. Former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon made a lot of noise this week with a viral thread on X. He has since talked to Wired and Axios .
